questions.text: 1932 में पूना पैक्ट किन दो नेताओं के मध्य हस्ताक्षरित किया गया था ?
questions.text_english: Between which two leaders was the Poona Pact signed in 1932?
questions.solution: The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932 between Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi. It was signed after Gandhi undertook a fast unto death protesting against the British government's decision to grant separate electorates for depressed classes. The pact reserved seats for depressed classes within the general electorate. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as Nehru, Lord Irwin, and Jinnah were not parties to this pact.
questions.solution_hindi: पूना पैक्ट सितंबर 1932 में डॉ. भीमराव अम्बेडकर और महात्मा गाँधी के बीच हस्ताक्षरित हुआ था। यह पैक्ट तब हुआ जब गाँधीजी ने दलित वर्गों के लिए पृथक निर्वाचन क्षेत्र के विरोध में आमरण अनशन किया। इस पैक्ट के तहत सामान्य निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में दलित वर्गों के लिए सीटें आरक्षित की गईं।

questions.text_english:
Two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): Giuseppe Mazzini was a revolutionary from Italy.
Reason (R): He founded underground organisations.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Giuseppe Mazzini was indeed a revolutionary from Italy who believed in the unification of Italy and worked toward this goal by founding secret societies such as 'Young Italy' and 'Young Europe'. His founding of underground organisations is directly linked to his revolutionary activities, making Reason (R) the correct explanation of Assertion (A). Therefore, option A is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। ज्युसेपे मेत्सिनी इटली के एक क्रांतिकारी थे जिन्होंने इटली के एकीकरण के लिए 'यंग इटली' और 'यंग यूरोप' जैसे गुप्त संगठनों की स्थापना की। इसलिए विकल्प A सही है।

questions.text_english: Which country was the most affected by the potato famine during 1845-1849?
questions.solution: Ireland was the most affected country by the Great Potato Famine (also known as the Great Hunger) during 1845–1849. The Irish population was heavily dependent on the potato as a staple food. When a potato blight destroyed crops for several consecutive years, it led to mass starvation and death, killing approximately one million people and forcing another million to emigrate. France, the USA, and Sweden were not as severely affected by this specific famine.

Arrange the following historical events in chronological order and choose the correct option:
I. Publication of Bengal Gazette
II. Publication of Diamond Sutra
III. Publication of Bible by Johann Gutenberg
IV. Return of Marco Polo to Italy from China
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is II, IV, III, I. The Diamond Sutra was printed in China in 868 CE, making it the world's oldest known printed book. Marco Polo returned to Italy from China around 1295 CE. Johann Gutenberg published the Bible using his printing press around 1448 CE. The Bengal Gazette, India's first newspaper, was published by James Augustus Hicky in 1780 CE. Therefore, option D (II, IV, III, I) is the correct chronological sequence.

questions.text: सोलहवीं शताब्दी के मध्य में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी घातक बीमारी पुर्तगाल और स्पेन से अमेरिका में फैली थी ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following deadly disease spread in America through Portugal and Spain in mid-sixteenth century?
questions.solution: Smallpox was the deadly disease that spread in America through Portuguese and Spanish colonisers in the mid-sixteenth century. The indigenous people of America had no immunity against smallpox as they had never been exposed to it before. This disease wiped out entire communities of native American populations, making European conquest far easier. Yellow fever, malaria, and cholera were not the primary disease brought by the Spanish and Portuguese that caused such catastrophic mortality among the native Americans.
questions.solution_hindi: चेचक वह घातक बीमारी थी जो सोलहवीं शताब्दी के मध्य में पुर्तगाल और स्पेन से अमेरिका में फैली। अमेरिका के मूल निवासियों में चेचक के प्रति कोई प्रतिरोधक क्षमता नहीं थी, जिससे उनकी बड़ी संख्या में मृत्यु हुई।

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the role of language in the development of nationalism in Poland during the nineteenth century.

key_points: Russian rulers suppressed Polish language to weaken national identity
Polish language became a symbol of resistance and national struggle
Church used Polish for religious instruction, keeping national spirit alive
Language linked people to their cultural roots and unified them against oppression

sub_questions.solution: In the nineteenth century, Poland was under Russian domination, and the Russian government imposed the Russian language on the Polish people. Polish was banned from schools and public life. However, the Polish language became a powerful symbol of national resistance. The Polish Catholic Church continued to use the Polish language for religious instruction and services, which helped keep the national identity and cultural spirit alive among the people. Many Poles were arrested and sent to Siberia for refusing to give up their language. This linguistic resistance strengthened the bonds among the Polish people and became a central force in the development of Polish nationalism and the struggle for independence.

sub_questions.text: 1815 की वियना संधि के मुख्य प्रावधानों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the main provisions of the Treaty of Vienna of 1815.

key_points: Restoration of conservative monarchies overthrown by Napoleon
France was stripped of territories it had annexed
Balance of power was established to prevent future French aggression
New conservative order was established in Europe

sub_questions.solution: The Treaty of Vienna of 1815 was drawn up by the conservative powers of Europe — Britain, Russia, Prussia, and Austria — after the defeat of Napoleon. The main provisions were: first, the Bourbon dynasty was restored to power in France, and conservative monarchies that had been overthrown by Napoleon were reinstated throughout Europe. Second, France was stripped of the territories it had annexed and was surrounded by a ring of strong states to prevent future aggression. Third, the principle of legitimacy was established, meaning that dynasties that had ruled before Napoleon were restored. Fourth, a new conservative order was created in Europe aimed at suppressing liberal and nationalist movements.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the expansion of the 'Non-Cooperation Movement' in the countryside.

key_points: Awadh peasants under Baba Ramchandra refused to pay high rents
Tribal communities in Andhra Pradesh led by Alluri Sitarama Raju took up arms
Farmers in Bardoli refused to pay revenue
Peasants' grievances linked to nationalist movement
Movement spread beyond urban areas into rural India

sub_questions.solution: The Non-Cooperation Movement spread rapidly to the countryside, drawing in different sections of rural society. In Awadh (present-day Uttar Pradesh), peasants under the leadership of Baba Ramchandra launched a movement against talukdars and landlords who charged high rents and forced peasants into unpaid labour (begar). Peasants demanded reduction of revenue, abolition of begar, and social boycott of oppressive landlords. In the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh, tribal communities under Alluri Sitarama Raju took up arms, blending the Gandhian non-cooperation idea with their own struggle against forest laws that restricted their way of life. In Bardoli (Gujarat), farmers refused to pay land revenue. These diverse rural movements, though rooted in local grievances, merged with the larger nationalist struggle and gave the Non-Cooperation Movement a truly mass character.

sub_questions.text_english: How did icons and symbols play an important role in the development of nationalism in India? Explain.

key_points: Bharat Mata image created sense of shared motherland
Swadeshi movement used Indian symbols to promote unity
Tricolour flag used during nationalist movement
Vande Mataram as national song became symbol of unity
Folk songs and imagery used to connect common people to nationalism

sub_questions.solution: Icons and symbols played a crucial role in developing a sense of national unity and patriotism among the Indian people. The image of Bharat Mata, painted by Abanindranath Tagore, depicted India as a divine mother figure and became a powerful symbol that stirred emotional attachment to the motherland among Indians across regions. During the Swadeshi movement, a tricolour flag with eight lotuses and a crescent moon was used as a symbol of national identity. Vande Mataram, composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, became an emotionally charged national song that united people against colonial rule. Nationalist leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak used the Ganesh festival and Shivaji festival as platforms to promote national consciousness and bring together large numbers of people in a shared cultural identity. These symbols transcended language and regional differences, creating a common national feeling.

1857 के विद्रोह के बाद प्रेस की स्वतंत्रता के प्रति औपनिवेशिक सरकार का रवैया बदल गया। कुछ अंग्रेजों ने 'देसी' प्रेस का मुँह बंद करने की माँग की। ज्यों-ज्यों भाषाई समाचार पत्र राष्ट्रवाद से समर्थन में मुखर होते गए, त्यों-त्यों औपनिवेशिक सरकार में कड़े नियंत्रण के प्रस्ताव पर बहस तेज़ होने लगी। आयरिश प्रेस कानून के तर्ज पर 1878 में वर्नाक्युलर प्रेस एक्ट लागू कर दिया गया। इससे सरकार को भाषाई प्रेस में छपी रपट और संपादकीय को सेंसर करने का व्यापक हक़ मिल गया। अब से सरकार ने विभिन्न प्रदेशों से छपने वाले भाषाई अखबारों पर नियमित नज़र रखनी शुरू कर दी। अगर किसी रपट को बाग़ी करार दिया जाता था तो अखबार को पहले चेतावनी दी जाती थी, और अगर चेतावनी की अनसुनी हुई, तो अखबार को जब्त किया जा सकता था और छपाई की मशीनें छीन ली जा सकती थीं।
questions.text_english:
Read the given source carefully and answer the questions that follow:

Print and Censorship

After the revolt of 1857, the attitude of the colonial government towards freedom of the press changed. Enraged Englishmen demanded a clamp down on the 'native' press. As vernacular newspapers became assertively nationalist, the colonial government began debating measures of stringent control. In 1878, the Vernacular Press Act was passed, modelled on the Irish Press Laws. It provided the government with extensive rights to censor reports and editorials in the vernacular press. From now on the government kept regular track of the vernacular newspapers published in different provinces. When a report was judged as seditious, the newspaper was warned, and if the warning was ignored, the press was liable to be seized and the printing machinery confiscated.

sub_questions.solution: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was modelled on the Irish Press Laws. The British government in India used the Irish Press Laws as a template to give themselves extensive powers to censor and suppress the vernacular (native language) press in India.

sub_questions.solution: The colonial government was not in favour of freedom of the press because vernacular newspapers were becoming increasingly assertive in their support for nationalism and were spreading anti-British sentiments among the Indian population. After the revolt of 1857, the British feared that a free native press could incite more rebellions and undermine colonial authority, so they sought to suppress it.

sub_questions.solution: The Vernacular Press Act gave the colonial government two important powers. First, it provided the government with extensive rights to censor reports and editorials published in the vernacular (native language) press. Second, if a report was judged as seditious and the newspaper ignored the government's warning, the government had the power to seize the newspaper and confiscate its printing machinery entirely.

questions.solution: Bamboo drip irrigation is a traditional and indigenous irrigation system practised in Meghalaya. In this system, bamboo pipes are used to divert and distribute water from streams and springs to fields, using the principle of gravity. It is a 200-year-old system used by the tribal communities of Meghalaya, particularly for watering betel leaf and black pepper vines. The other states — Himachal Pradesh, Kerala, and Rajasthan — do not use this specific system.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe the main provisions of 'Joint Forest Management'.

key_points: Local communities and government jointly manage forests
Communities get usufruct rights like collection of non-timber forest products
Communities protect forests in return for benefits

sub_questions.solution: Joint Forest Management (JFM) is a programme introduced in India in 1988 that involves local village communities working alongside the government Forest Department to protect and manage degraded forest land. Under this programme, village forest protection committees are formed that guard the forests. In return, the communities get usufruct rights — the right to collect non-timber forest products such as fruits, seeds, and medicinal plants. They also receive a share of the timber when the forest is harvested. This approach ensures sustainable forest management and directly benefits local communities.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe any two characteristics of 'protected forests' in India.

key_points: Forest land is protected from further depletion
Some activities like grazing and collection of forest produce are allowed with restrictions

sub_questions.solution: Protected forests in India are those forest areas declared protected by the Forest Department under the Indian Forest Act. First, these forests are safeguarded against any further depletion, and no new agricultural clearance is permitted within them. Second, limited activities such as controlled grazing and collection of minor forest produce may be permitted in protected forests, but these are regulated by the Forest Department to ensure the forests are not damaged. Protected forests constitute about one-third of the total classified forest area in India.

questions.text: भू-संरक्षण हेतु कोई तीन उपाय सुझाइए।
questions.text_english: Suggest any three measures for conservation of land.

key_points: Afforestation and planting shelter belts to prevent soil erosion
Proper management of grazing to control overgrazing
Reclamation of wasteland through scientific methods

questions.solution: Three important measures for the conservation of land are as follows. First, afforestation and planting of shelter belts (rows of trees) help prevent soil erosion caused by wind and water, thereby protecting land from degradation. Second, controlling overgrazing by implementing rotational grazing practices and regulating the number of livestock on pasture lands helps prevent land from becoming barren. Third, wasteland reclamation through scientific methods such as filling of gullies, construction of contour bunds, and strip cropping helps restore degraded land to productive use. Additionally, proper disposal of industrial and urban waste also prevents contamination and degradation of land.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the role of manufacturing industries in the economic development of a country.

key_points: Manufacturing creates employment opportunities
It increases national income and per capita income
It reduces dependence on primary sector and diversifies economy
It promotes modernisation and use of technology
It earns foreign exchange through export of manufactured goods

sub_questions.solution: Manufacturing industries play a vital role in the economic development of a country. First, they generate large-scale employment opportunities, both directly in factories and indirectly in supporting services, thereby reducing unemployment and improving living standards. Second, manufacturing contributes significantly to national income and GDP, helping to raise per capita income. Third, it transforms raw materials into finished goods, adding value and reducing dependence on the primary sector (agriculture). Fourth, modern manufacturing promotes the use of technology and innovation, leading to modernisation of the economy. Fifth, manufactured goods can be exported to earn valuable foreign exchange, which strengthens the country's economy. Countries like Japan, Germany, China, and South Korea have demonstrated that a strong manufacturing base is the foundation of economic prosperity and global competitiveness.

sub_questions.text: औद्योगिक प्रदूषण के विभिन्न प्रकारों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Analyse the different types of industrial pollution.

key_points: Air pollution from smoke and toxic gases released by factories
Water pollution from discharge of effluents into rivers and lakes
Land/soil pollution from dumping of industrial waste
Noise pollution from heavy machinery and industrial operations
Thermal pollution from hot water discharge into water bodies

sub_questions.solution: Industrial pollution affects the environment in several ways. Air pollution is caused when industries release smoke, dust, and toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide into the atmosphere, harming human health and causing acid rain. Water pollution occurs when industries discharge untreated chemical effluents, heavy metals, and dyes into rivers, lakes, and groundwater, making water unfit for drinking and aquatic life. Land pollution results from the dumping of solid industrial waste and hazardous chemicals on land, which degrades soil quality and contaminates groundwater. Noise pollution is caused by the operation of heavy machinery, generators, and industrial equipment, leading to hearing loss and stress. Thermal pollution occurs when industries discharge hot water into water bodies, raising water temperature and harming aquatic ecosystems. All these forms of pollution require strict regulation and treatment before discharge.

options.A: सभी वर्गों की सत्ता में साझेदारी सुनिश्चित करना।
options.B: सिंहली को राज भाषा घोषित करना।
options.C: तमिल को राज भाषा घोषित करना।

options_english.C: Declaring Tamil as the official language.
options_english.D: Implementing a policy of preference for Sinhalese in government jobs.

questions.solution: In 1956, the Sri Lankan government passed an Act that declared Sinhala as the only official language, ignoring the Tamil language entirely. This decision was deeply resented by the Tamil-speaking minority who felt that they were being treated as second-class citizens. It led to protests, discrimination in education and employment, and eventually escalated into a prolonged civil war between the Sinhalese-dominated government and Tamil militant groups like the LTTE. Option A is opposite to what happened; options C and D, while also contributing factors, were not the specific change of the 1956 law that sparked the civil conflict.

questions.text_english: Which one of the following countries is an example of a 'coming together federation'?
questions.solution: Australia is an example of a 'coming together federation'. In this type of federation, independent states come together voluntarily and pool their sovereignty to form a bigger unit (federation) while retaining their individual identities. The USA, Switzerland, and Australia are classic examples. India is a 'holding together federation' where a large country divides itself into constituent units. Belgium and Spain are also 'holding together' federations. Therefore, option D (Australia) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: ऑस्ट्रेलिया 'साथ आकर संघ बनाने' का उदाहरण है। इस प्रकार के संघ में स्वतंत्र राज्य मिलकर एक बड़ी इकाई बनाते हैं। अमेरिका, ऑस्ट्रेलिया और स्विट्ज़रलैंड इसके उदाहरण हैं। भारत 'साथ रहकर संघ बनाने' का उदाहरण है।

questions.text_english: Suggest any two reforms to strengthen 'party system' in India.

key_points: Internal democracy within parties — parties should hold regular internal elections
State funding of elections to reduce the influence of money and corruption

questions.solution: Two important reforms to strengthen the party system in India are as follows. First, there should be greater internal democracy within political parties, meaning parties must hold regular and transparent internal elections for leadership positions and give ordinary members a real say in decision-making, reducing dynastic politics. Second, state funding of elections should be introduced to reduce the dependence of parties on rich donors and corporate funding, which would help curb corruption and ensure a more level playing field for all political parties in elections.

questions.text: "शिकायतों का बने रहना लोकतंत्र की सफलता की गवाही देता है।" उदाहरणों सहित इस कथन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: "Complaints are the testimony to the success of Democracy." Explain the statement with examples.

key_points: In a democracy, citizens have the freedom to voice complaints, which itself is a sign of a healthy democracy
The existence of complaints shows awareness among citizens and functioning of free speech

questions.solution: This statement means that the very existence of complaints in a democracy proves that the system is working. In a democracy, citizens are free to express dissatisfaction with the government without fear of punishment, which itself is a sign of freedom. For example, in India, citizens can protest against government policies, file petitions in courts, and criticise leaders in the media. This freedom of expression does not exist in authoritarian regimes. The ability to complain and demand better governance shows that democracy empowers people, making complaints a testimony to its success rather than its failure.
questions.solution_hindi: इस कथन का अर्थ है कि लोकतंत्र में शिकायतें करने का अधिकार ही इसकी सफलता का प्रमाण है। भारत में नागरिक सरकार की नीतियों के विरुद्ध विरोध कर सकते हैं, न्यायालय में जा सकते हैं और मीडिया में आलोचना कर सकते हैं। यह अधिकार तानाशाही में नहीं होता।

questions.text: संघवाद की प्रमुख विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the main features of federalism.

key_points: Two or more levels of government
Each level has its own jurisdiction with clear division of powers
Constitution is supreme and changes require consent of both levels
Courts have power to interpret constitution and protect division of powers
Revenue resources are specified for each level

questions.solution: Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central (national) government and various regional (state) governments. The main features of federalism are: first, there are two or more levels of government, each governing the same citizens but with different jurisdictions. Second, the division of powers is clearly defined in the Constitution, and neither level can override the other's authority in its own sphere. Third, the Constitution is supreme, and any changes to the fundamental division of powers require the consent of both levels of government. Fourth, courts have the power to interpret the Constitution and resolve disputes between different levels of government. Fifth, sources of revenue are clearly specified for each level to ensure financial autonomy.
questions.solution_hindi: संघवाद एक शासन प्रणाली है जिसमें सत्ता केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच बँटी होती है। इसकी विशेषताएँ: सरकार के दो या अधिक स्तर, शक्तियों का स्पष्ट विभाजन, संविधान की सर्वोच्चता, न्यायालय का संवैधानिक विवादों में निर्णय और प्रत्येक स्तर के लिए अलग राजस्व स्रोत।

(a) Compare the Belgian model and the Sri Lankan model of power sharing.
OR
(b) Why is power sharing necessary in a democracy? Explain.

sub_questions.text_english: Compare the Belgian model and the Sri Lankan model of power sharing.

key_points: Belgium recognised diversity and accommodated all communities
Sri Lanka ignored minority Tamil community's aspirations
Belgium followed power-sharing leading to peace and unity
Sri Lanka's majoritarian approach led to civil war
Belgium is a success story; Sri Lanka is a cautionary tale

sub_questions.solution: Belgium and Sri Lanka adopted completely different models of power sharing, leading to very different outcomes. Belgium had a complex ethnic composition with Dutch-speaking Flemish (59%), French-speaking Walloons (40%), and a small German-speaking community. Rather than allowing majority rule to dominate, Belgium worked out a unique power-sharing arrangement. Equal representation was given to both Dutch and French speakers in the central cabinet, regional governments were given autonomy, and a community government was established for cultural matters. This accommodative approach prevented conflict and helped Belgium remain united as a peaceful democracy. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, adopted a majoritarian approach after independence. The Sinhala majority imposed its language and religion on the Tamil minority, leading to alienation, resentment, and ultimately a prolonged civil war lasting decades. Thus, Belgium's inclusive model stands in stark contrast to Sri Lanka's exclusive model.

sub_questions.text: लोकतंत्र में सत्ता की साझेदारी क्यों आवश्यक है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Why is power sharing necessary in a democracy? Explain.

key_points: Reduces conflict among various social groups
Prevents concentration of power leading to tyranny
Ensures stability and unity in diverse societies
Promotes participation of all sections of society
Upholds the spirit of democracy

sub_questions.solution: Power sharing is essential in a democracy for several important reasons. First, it reduces the possibility of conflict between different social, ethnic, and linguistic groups. When every group feels that it has a share in governance, it does not feel excluded or oppressed, reducing social tensions. Second, power sharing prevents the concentration of power in the hands of one person or group, which could lead to tyranny and the abuse of authority. Third, in diverse countries like India, power sharing ensures that the voices of different regions and communities are represented in decision-making, promoting national unity and integrity. Fourth, it upholds the very spirit of democracy, which is based on the idea that political power ultimately belongs to all the people. The example of Belgium shows that inclusive power sharing leads to peace and progress, while Sri Lanka's majoritarian approach led to conflict and instability.

कई देशों में सिर्फ एक ही दल को सरकार बनाने और चलाने की अनुमति है। इस कारण उन्हें एकदलीय शासन-व्यवस्था कहा जाता है। कुछ देशों में सत्ता आमतौर पर दो मुख्य दलों के बीच ही बदलती रहती है। वहाँ अनेक दूसरी पार्टियाँ हो सकती हैं, वे भी चुनाव लड़कर कुछ सीटें जीत सकती हैं पर सिर्फ दो ही दल बहुमत पाने और सरकार बनाने के प्रबल दावेदार होते हैं। इसे द्वि-दलीय व्यवस्था कहा जाता है। जब अनेक दल सत्ता के लिए होड़ में हों और दो दलों से ज्यादा के लिए या तो अपने दम पर या दूसरों से गठबंधन करके सत्ता में आने का ठीक-ठाक अवसर हो तो इसे हम बहुदलीय व्यवस्था कहते हैं।
questions.text_english:

How many political parties?

In some countries, only one party is allowed to control and run the government. These are called one-party systems. In some countries, power usually changes between two main parties. Several other parties may exist, contest elections and win a few seats in the national legislatures. Such a party system is called two-party system. If several parties compete for power, and more than two parties have a reasonable chance of coming to power either on their own strength or in alliance with others, we call it a multiparty system.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the main feature of 'multi-party system'.

key_points: In a multi-party system, several parties compete for power and more than two parties have a reasonable chance of coming to power on their own or in alliance.

sub_questions.solution: The main feature of a multi-party system is that several parties compete for political power, and more than two parties have a realistic chance of coming to power either on their own strength or by forming alliances or coalitions with other parties. India is an example of a multi-party system where regional and national parties combine to form coalition governments.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is a 'one-party system' not compatible with democracy?

key_points: A one-party system is not compatible with democracy because it denies citizens the freedom to choose between alternatives and eliminates competition, accountability, and political freedom.

sub_questions.solution: A one-party system is not compatible with democracy because democracy requires that citizens have the freedom to choose their government through free and fair elections with genuine alternatives. In a one-party system, no competition exists, so citizens cannot vote the ruling party out of power. This eliminates accountability, suppresses opposition, and denies citizens political freedoms, which are the very foundations of a democratic system.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the main characteristics of a coalition government.

key_points: Formed when no single party gets a majority
Multiple parties come together to form government
Based on a common minimum programme
Requires compromise and coordination among partners

sub_questions.solution: A coalition government is formed in a multi-party system when no single party wins a majority of seats in the legislature. The main characteristics are: first, it is formed by an alliance of two or more political parties that together have enough seats to form a majority government. Second, the coalition partners agree on a Common Minimum Programme outlining the policies they will jointly pursue. Third, it requires constant negotiation, compromise, and coordination among partner parties, which can sometimes make governance slower but also more representative. India has experienced coalition governments at the national level since 1989.

questions.text: भारत में विनिमय के माध्यम के रूप में रुपए को ही स्वीकार क्यों किया जाता है ?
questions.text_english: Why is Rupee accepted as a medium of exchange in India?

options.A: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा राज्य सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।
options.B: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा केन्द्र सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।
options.C: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय स्टेट बैंक द्वारा केन्द्र सरकार की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।
options.D: क्योंकि इसे भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक द्वारा विश्व बैंक की ओर से जारी किया जाता है।

options_english.A: Because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the State Government.
options_english.B: Because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government.
options_english.C: Because it is issued by the State Bank of India on behalf of the Central Government.
options_english.D: Because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the World Bank.

questions.solution: The Rupee is accepted as a medium of exchange in India because it is issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on behalf of the Central Government of India. The currency is authorised by law, making it legal tender — meaning no one can legally refuse to accept it as payment. The RBI has the sole authority to issue currency notes in India. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because the State Government, State Bank of India, and World Bank do not have the authority to issue Indian currency.

questions.text_english: Why do some countries impose tariffs on imported goods in the context of globalization? Choose the correct reason from the following options:

options.A: मुक्त व्यापार का समर्थन करने के लिए
options.B: स्थानीय उद्योगों की रक्षा करने के लिए
options.D: आयात लागत कम करने के लिए

questions.solution: Some countries impose tariffs (taxes on imported goods) in the context of globalisation primarily to protect their local industries from foreign competition. When cheaper foreign goods flood a domestic market, local manufacturers cannot compete and may be forced to shut down, causing unemployment. By imposing tariffs, the government makes imported goods more expensive, allowing local industries to compete on more equal terms. This is called trade protectionism. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because imposing tariffs does the opposite of supporting free trade, does not directly attract investment, and actually raises rather than lowers import costs.

Two statements labelled as Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Read both the statements carefully and choose the correct option:

Reason (R): Tertiary sector is called as service sector.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Since the Assertion is false but the Reason is true, option D is the correct answer.

questions.text: ऋण लेने में समर्थक ऋणाधार का उद्देश्य निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is the purpose of collateral in a loan?

options.B: ऋणदाता के लिए ऋण सुरक्षित करना
options.C: ऋणदाता के लिए कागजी दस्तावेज़ कम करना

options_english.A: To increase the interest for the lender
options_english.B: To secure the loan for the lender
options_english.C: To reduce paperwork for the lender
options_english.D: To avoid repayment on the loan

questions.solution: The purpose of collateral in a loan is to secure the loan for the lender. Collateral is an asset (such as land, building, vehicle, livestock, or deposits with banks) that the borrower owns and pledges to the lender as security against the loan. If the borrower fails to repay the loan, the lender has the right to sell the collateral asset to recover the loan amount. This protects the lender from the risk of non-repayment. Options A, C, and D are incorrect as collateral does not increase interest, reduce paperwork, or help the borrower avoid repayment.
questions.solution_hindi: ऋणाधार (Collateral) का उद्देश्य ऋणदाता के लिए ऋण सुरक्षित करना है। ऋणी अपनी संपत्ति को ऋणाधार के रूप में गिरवी रखता है। यदि वह ऋण नहीं चुका पाता तो ऋणदाता उस संपत्ति को बेचकर ऋण वसूल कर सकता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रक का उदाहरण है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is an example of public sector?
questions.solution: Indian Railways is an example of the public sector because it is owned, operated, and managed by the Government of India. In the public sector, the government owns and operates enterprises using public money, and the primary aim is public welfare rather than profit. Birla Cement, Tata Iron and Steel Company, and Reliance Industries Limited are all private sector companies owned by private individuals and corporations with the primary aim of making profit.
questions.solution_hindi: भारतीय रेलवे सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रक का उदाहरण है क्योंकि यह भारत सरकार के स्वामित्व और प्रबंधन में है। सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रक में सरकार की स्वामित्व होती है और उसका उद्देश्य जन-कल्याण होता है। बाकी तीन निजी क्षेत्रक की कंपनियाँ हैं।

questions.text: श्रीमती दीप्ति X देश की निवासी हैं। उनका देश एक विकसित देश है। उसके देश की निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी एक विशेषता होगी ?
questions.text_english: Smt. Deepti is a resident of X country. Her country is a developed country. Which of the following would be a characteristic of her country?
questions.solution: A developed country is characterised by a high per capita income. Developed countries like the USA, Germany, Japan, and Australia have high average incomes, high standards of living, and high Human Development Index scores. Options A, C, and D — high infant mortality rate, low literacy rate, and low net attendance ratio — are all characteristics of underdeveloped or developing countries, not developed ones. Therefore, option B (High Per Capita Income) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: एक विकसित देश की विशेषता उच्च प्रति व्यक्ति आय है। विकसित देशों में जीवन स्तर उच्च होता है। उच्च शिशु मृत्यु दर, निम्न साक्षरता दर और निम्न उपस्थिति अनुपात विकासशील या अल्पविकसित देशों की विशेषताएँ हैं।

questions.text: अर्थव्यवस्था के 'द्वितीयक क्षेत्रक' की प्रमुख विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the main characteristics of the 'secondary sector' of the economy.

key_points: Secondary sector involves manufacturing and processing of goods
It transforms raw materials (primary sector output) into finished products

questions.solution: The secondary sector of the economy, also known as the industrial sector, has the following main characteristics. First, it involves manufacturing and processing activities that transform raw materials obtained from the primary sector into finished or semi-finished products. For example, cotton (primary sector) is converted into cloth (secondary sector), or iron ore is turned into steel. Second, it includes industries such as textiles, steel, automobiles, cement, chemicals, and food processing. The secondary sector contributes significantly to a country's GDP and provides employment to large numbers of workers in factories and manufacturing units.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वितीयक क्षेत्रक (औद्योगिक क्षेत्रक) की विशेषताएँ: पहला, यह क्षेत्रक प्राथमिक क्षेत्रक से प्राप्त कच्चे माल को विनिर्माण और प्रसंस्करण द्वारा तैयार वस्तुओं में बदलता है। दूसरा, इसमें कपड़ा, इस्पात, सीमेंट, ऑटोमोबाइल जैसे उद्योग शामिल हैं।

questions.text: संगठित क्षेत्रक की प्रमुख विशेषताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Explain the main characteristics of the organised sector.

key_points: Registered with the government and follows official rules and regulations
Workers get job security, fixed working hours, and social security benefits
Employees receive paid leave, provident fund, and other benefits

questions.solution: The organised sector has several important characteristics. First, enterprises in the organised sector are registered with the government and are required to follow its rules and regulations as laid down in various laws such as the Factories Act, Minimum Wages Act, and Provident Fund Act. Second, workers in the organised sector enjoy job security, meaning they cannot be dismissed without a valid reason or proper procedure. Third, they work fixed and regulated hours, with overtime pay for extra work. Fourth, they receive various social security benefits such as paid leave, provident fund, gratuity, medical benefits, and pension. These benefits provide workers a much more secure and stable livelihood compared to unorganised sector workers.
questions.solution_hindi: संगठित क्षेत्रक की विशेषताएँ: पहला, उद्यम सरकार में पंजीकृत हैं और कानूनों का पालन करते हैं। दूसरा, श्रमिकों को नौकरी की सुरक्षा होती है। तीसरा, नियमित कार्यघंटे और वेतन मिलता है। चौथा, भविष्य निधि, चिकित्सा सुविधा, अवकाश वेतन जैसी सुविधाएँ मिलती हैं।

questions.text: 'शरीर द्रव्यमान सूचकांक' को परिभाषित कीजिए। इसकी गणना करने की विधि की व्याख्या कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Define the term 'Body Mass Index'. Explain the method of its calculation.

key_points: BMI is a measure used to determine whether a person is underweight, normal, overweight or obese
BMI = Weight (in kg) divided by Height squared (in metres)
BMI below 18.5 is underweight; 18.5-24.9 is normal; above 25 is overweight

questions.solution: Body Mass Index (BMI) is a numerical value that is used to assess whether a person's body weight is appropriate for their height, and to determine if they are underweight, normal weight, overweight, or obese. It is widely used as an indicator of nutritional status and overall health. The method of calculation is: BMI = Weight of the person in kilograms divided by the square of their height in metres. That is, BMI = Weight (kg) ÷ [Height (m)]². For example, if a person weighs 60 kg and is 1.5 m tall, their BMI = 60 ÷ (1.5 × 1.5) = 60 ÷ 2.25 = 26.7. A BMI below 18.5 is considered underweight, 18.5 to 24.9 is normal, and above 25 is considered overweight.
questions.solution_hindi: शरीर द्रव्यमान सूचकांक (BMI) एक संख्यात्मक मान है जो किसी व्यक्ति की ऊँचाई के अनुपात में उसके वजन का आकलन करता है। गणना विधि: BMI = वजन (किलोग्राम में) ÷ [ऊँचाई (मीटर में)]²। यदि BMI 18.5 से कम है तो कम वजन, 18.5-24.9 सामान्य और 25 से अधिक है तो अधिक वजन माना जाता है।

(a) Differentiate between the formal and informal sources of credit.
OR

sub_questions.text: साख के औपचारिक एवं अनौपचारिक स्रोतों में अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between the formal and informal sources of credit.

key_points: Formal sources include banks and cooperatives; informal sources include moneylenders, traders, and relatives
Formal sources are regulated by RBI; informal sources have no regulation
Formal sources charge lower interest; informal sources charge very high interest
Formal sources require collateral and documentation; informal sources are more flexible but exploitative
Formal credit helps development; informal credit can trap borrowers in a debt cycle

sub_questions.solution: Formal sources of credit include banks (nationalised and commercial), cooperative societies, and other financial institutions regulated by the Reserve Bank of India. These sources charge relatively lower and fixed rates of interest, are subject to government supervision, and must follow proper lending procedures. However, they often require collateral and extensive paperwork, which makes it difficult for poor people to access them. Informal sources of credit include moneylenders, traders, landlords, friends, and relatives. These sources are not regulated by any authority and can charge very high rates of interest, sometimes exploiting borrowers. They do not require formal documentation, making them more accessible to the poor, but this often traps borrowers in a cycle of debt. The government promotes formal credit to reduce dependence on exploitative informal sources and to ensure that more people can access affordable credit for productive purposes.

sub_questions.text: 'स्वयं-सहायता समूहों' की कार्यप्रणाली को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the functioning of 'Self-Help Groups'.

key_points: A group of 15-20 members from poor households who pool savings
Members can take small loans from the group at low interest
After regular savings, the group can borrow from banks
Decisions taken collectively by group members
Helps empower rural poor, especially women

sub_questions.solution: Self-Help Groups (SHGs) are small informal groups of 15 to 20 people, mostly from poor households in rural areas, who come together to help each other financially and socially. The functioning of SHGs is as follows: members meet regularly and each member saves a small amount of money — even as little as a few rupees per month. These savings are pooled together, and members can borrow small amounts from this common pool for urgent needs at a reasonable rate of interest. Decisions regarding savings, loans, and interest rates are made collectively by the group members through democratic discussion. Once the group has demonstrated a good track record of regular savings and repayment, it can approach a bank to borrow a larger loan under the micro-credit linkage programme. The bank loan is then lent out to members who need it. SHGs have been particularly effective in empowering rural women, helping them become financially independent and making collective decisions about their lives.
